competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Describe the position of objects in space
indicatorDescription: Tell the position of objects relative to other objects in space using positional words.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: tell the position of objects relative to other objects in space using positional words.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom furniture; toys; PE cones; positional picture cards; boxes and small toys
keywords: position of objects, relative, above, below, to the right, to the left, in front of, behind, next to
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 2. position and space.'
Write today's key term 'position of objects' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Follow-the-position instructions drill; relative position Q&A; classroom map sketch

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

contentStandardDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as a part of a whole
indicatorDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and model the concept of: understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Paper sheets (circles, rectangles); real apples, oranges, or loaves of bread; safety plastic scissors; play dough; fraction bars
keywords: fraction, one-half, half, whole, equal parts, partition, divide
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a fun number song like '1, 2, Buckle My Shoe' or 'Ten Green Bottles' with clapping.
Have pupils do a quick oral counting exercise from 1 to 20, first forwards and then backwards.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin learning about 3. fractions using real counters.'
Write today's key words on the board: 'fraction' and read it aloud together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models. Displays concrete counters (stones, bottle caps) or ten-frames. Shows how to count, add, subtract or partition a whole group clearly.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Concrete Practice - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups. Teacher gives each group a bundle of counters and guides them to repeat the count, addition, or subtraction.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Discovery - 7 min): Groups solve simple concrete puzzles (e.g. making groups of 5, matching coins to values, or folding paper to show halves).
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher monitors groups, correcting hand placements on counters, and reinforcing mathematical vocabulary.
plenary: Whole class sings a joyful counting song together with body actions.
Ask: 'What did we learn to count or do today?' (Have 2-3 pupils explain).
Homework: 'Find 10 small objects at home (seeds, bottle caps) and count them to your parents.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson: we will write and draw our numbers!
assessment: Practical paper-folding task; coloring half-shapes worksheet; oral identification of halves

contentStandardDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as a part of a whole
indicatorDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to practice and represent: understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Paper sheets (circles, rectangles); real apples, oranges, or loaves of bread; safety plastic scissors; play dough; fraction bars
keywords: fraction, one-half, half, whole, equal parts, partition, divide
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 3. fractions.'
Write the key words 'fraction, one-half' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Practical paper-folding task; coloring half-shapes worksheet; oral identification of halves

rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'

NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'

Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 4. money.'
Write the key words 'recognise, ghanaian coins' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Role-play shop transaction; coin-recognition quiz; matching coins to prices worksheet

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of measuring as a process of comparing
indicatorDescription: Develop an understanding of measuring as a process of comparing pairs of items using comparative words.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explore and solve tasks on: develop an understanding of measuring as a process of comparing pairs of items using comparative words.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pairs of classroom objects (books, pencils, desks, cups, boxes); balance scales (toy); water basins; height charts
keywords: measuring, comparing pairs, smaller, longer, thinner, heavier, bigger, taller, lighter, thicker
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 3. measurement.'
Write today's key term 'measuring' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Practical comparison task; result table construction; comparison oral check

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise a given set of data into three categories, find the total number of data points and determine how many are in each category and compare the number in any two categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explore and solve tasks on: organise a given set of data into three categories, find the total number of data points and determine how many are in each category and compare the number in any two categories.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Tally sheets; grid paper; colored pencils; cut-out picture cards for pictographs; counters of different colors
keywords: organise data, three categories, total data points, determine quantity, compare categories, difference, most, least
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise data' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Data-reading worksheet; tallies-to-pictograph project; group comparison report

ACTIVITY 3 (Drawing & Sorting - 7 min): Pupils return to the classroom and draw 2 living things and 2 non-living things in their notebooks, coloring them.
ACTIVITY 4 (Discussion & Sharing - 3 min): Selected pupils show their drawings to the class and describe one feature. Teacher reinforces concepts using mother tongue where necessary.

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicatorDescription: Identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Human body chart; mirrors; pictures of body parts; senses-station activity (objects to feel, hear, see, smell, taste); 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' song
keywords: identify, external, human, body, parts, appropriate, names, senses
rpk: Learners are aware of their own body, hands, eyes, nose, and mouth, and use them daily.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' together with rapid physical actions.
Play 'Simon Says' to identify and touch external body parts quickly.
Recall why we need our body parts to work interdependently to play and learn.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice identifying and describing our 1. the human body systems.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Body Parts Game - 5 min): Play an accelerated game of 'Simon Says' or point to body parts to test speed and accuracy. Pupils clap for correct answers.

ACTIVITY 2 (Senses Exploration - 5 min): In small groups, pupils explore different sense objects (rough stone, smelling flower, hearing bell, tasting safely). They identify which body part is responsible.
ACTIVITY 3 (Human Body Chart - 7 min): In small groups, pupils paste labels (eyes, ears, hand, chest, shoulders, leg) onto a large blank outline of a human body.
ACTIVITY 4 (Feedback & Review - 3 min): Each group displays their body chart. Teacher provides positive feedback and reinforces vocabulary: identify, external, human.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical body parts labeling; class exercise (classification table); Simon Says game

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources
indicatorDescription: Understand energy and give examples of its uses.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: understand energy and give examples of its uses.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation
resources: Torch; candle; battery; drum/bell; pictures of energy sources (sun, food, fuel); toy car
keywords: understand, energy, give, examples, uses, light, sound, heat, electricity
rpk: Learners have played with moving toys, felt heat, and seen lights and electrical appliances at home.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.
Have pupils stand up, push their chairs in, and then pull them out. Ask: 'What forces did we just use?'
Recall how energy and forces make objects move or make work easier.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will review and consolidate our understanding of 1. sources and forms of energy.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Forces/Energy Recap - 5 min): Teacher displays a toy machine, ramp, or electronic device. Pupils call out what force or energy it uses or how it helps us.
ACTIVITY 2 (Hands-on Ramps/Cars - 5 min): In small groups, pupils roll toy cars on smooth and rough surfaces to observe movement. They describe which surface has less resistance.
ACTIVITY 3 (Practical Investigation - 7 min): Pupils use simple materials (balloons, cardboard, rubber bands) to explore pushes, pulls, and energy. They draw their findings in their notebooks.
ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical demonstration; class exercise (identifying energy uses in the classroom)

contentStandardDescription: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicatorDescription: Explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
competencies: Personal Development & Leadership; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Soap; sponge; towel; bucket; basin; tippy-tap; water; hygiene poster showing bathing steps; doll/toy for bathing roleplay
keywords: explain, need, bathing, cleanliness, health, germs, how, done, soap
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners. Sing an active hygiene song like 'This is the way we wash our hands/brush our teeth.'
Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 1. personal hygiene and sanitation.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.
ACTIVITY 2 (Roleplay & Practice - 5 min): In small groups, pupils practice the 6-step handwashing technique using a real bar of soap and clean basins (or dry run) or roleplay brushing teeth.
ACTIVITY 3 (Surroundings Cleanup - 7 min): Pupils play a cleanup game, picking up safe trash (paper, plastic) in the classroom/schoolyard and sorting it into correct organic/inorganic bins.
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Oral Q&A; bathing roleplay/demonstration; short-answer test

contentStandardDescription: Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicatorDescription: Observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Plant specimens; pictures of trees/flowers; garden visit; hand lens; Ecosystem chart; community walk; pictures of different habitats
keywords: observe, describe, different, kinds, things, environment
rpk: Learners have seen various plants, animals, and non-living objects in their school and home environment.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Begin with a local call-and-response song about the natural world around us.
Play a 3-minute game of 'I Spy' where pupils spot a living or non-living thing in the classroom.
Review key words from previous sessions: observe, describe, different.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we are going to review and show what we know about 1. living and non-living things.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Interactive Review - 5 min): Teacher displays living and non-living objects (or cards). Pupils call out 'Living!' or 'Non-living!' in unison and explain why.
ACTIVITY 2 (Pair sorting - 5 min): In pairs, pupils sort physical specimens (leaves, twigs, plastic pens, stones) on their desks. Teacher checks and guides.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Challenge - 7 min): Groups are given cards of natural and man-made materials. They play a race game to sort them into correct trays.
ACTIVITY 4 (Consolidation - 3 min): Teacher clarifies any misconceptions, reviews the key term 'observe', and praises excellent team effort.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Observation worksheet; teacher observation rubric

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that some events in our environment occur recurrently
indicatorDescription: Explain that some natural phenomena, such as day and night, occur repeatedly.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: explain that some natural phenomena, such as day and night, occur repeatedly.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Pictures of sun, moon, sky; weather chart; flashlight (for sun-moon demo); globe or ball
keywords: explain, natural, phenomena, day, night, occur, repeatedly
rpk: Learners experience day and night daily, and see rain, sun, wind, and clouds in their daily lives.
starter: Greet learners. Recite a fun weather poem together: 'Sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, we love all weather!' with physical gestures.
Ask: 'What changes did you see in the sky on your way to school today?'
Review yesterday's lesson: the recurring natural events in our immediate environment.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice and show what we have learned about 1. earth science.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Weather/Day-Night Recap - 5 min): Teacher displays weather symbols on the board. Pupils match them to words (sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy) and discuss how they change.
ACTIVITY 2 (Interactive Demonstration - 5 min): Teacher uses a globe/ball and flashlight to demonstrate the repeating day and night cycle. Pupils take turns holding the light.
ACTIVITY 3 (Worksheet / Matching - 7 min): Pupils complete a matching worksheet, matching day/night to activities (e.g., sleeping at night, playing during the day) or matching weather to clothing.
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher corrects common errors on the worksheets and summarizes the natural cycle of 1. earth science.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Oral Q&A; short-answer test (5 marks); drawing of day and night scenes

starter: Greet learners warmly. Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' together with rapid physical actions.

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources
indicatorDescription: Understand energy and give examples of its uses.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: understand energy and give examples of its uses.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation
resources: Torch; candle; battery; drum/bell; pictures of energy sources (sun, food, fuel); toy car
keywords: understand, energy, give, examples, uses, light, sound, heat, electricity
rpk: Learners have played with moving toys, felt heat, and seen lights and electrical appliances at home.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.
Have pupils stand up, push their chairs in, and then pull them out. Ask: 'What forces did we just use?'
Recall how energy and forces make objects move or make work easier.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will review and consolidate our understanding of 1. sources and forms of energy.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Forces/Energy Recap - 5 min): Teacher displays a toy machine, ramp, or electronic device. Pupils call out what force or energy it uses or how it helps us.
ACTIVITY 2 (Hands-on Ramps/Cars - 5 min): In small groups, pupils roll toy cars on smooth and rough surfaces to observe movement. They describe which surface has less resistance.
ACTIVITY 3 (Practical Investigation - 7 min): Pupils use simple materials (balloons, cardboard, rubber bands) to explore pushes, pulls, and energy. They draw their findings in their notebooks.
ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical demonstration; class exercise (identifying energy uses in the classroom)

contentStandardDescription: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicatorDescription: Explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: explain the need for bathing and know how it is done.
competencies: Personal Development & Leadership; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Soap; sponge; towel; bucket; basin; tippy-tap; water; hygiene poster showing bathing steps; doll/toy for bathing roleplay
keywords: explain, need, bathing, cleanliness, health, germs, how, done, soap
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners. Sing an active hygiene song like 'This is the way we wash our hands/brush our teeth.'
Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 1. personal hygiene and sanitation.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.
ACTIVITY 2 (Roleplay & Practice - 5 min): In small groups, pupils practice the 6-step handwashing technique using a real bar of soap and clean basins (or dry run) or roleplay brushing teeth.
ACTIVITY 3 (Surroundings Cleanup - 7 min): Pupils play a cleanup game, picking up safe trash (paper, plastic) in the classroom/schoolyard and sorting it into correct organic/inorganic bins.
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Oral Q&A; bathing roleplay/demonstration; short-answer test

ACTIVITY 4 (Discussion & Sharing - 3 min): Selected pupils show their drawings to the class and describe one feature. Teacher reinforces concepts using mother tongue where necessary.

starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.

competencies: Personal Development & Leadership; Cultural Identity & Global Citizenship
resources: Soap; clean running water; tippy-tap or tap; clean towel or air dry; handwashing poster (NaCCA/WHO standard steps); glitter (germ simulation)
keywords: demonstrate, understanding, need, handwashing, germs, health, soap, running, water
rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners. Sing an active hygiene song like 'This is the way we wash our hands/brush our teeth.'
Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 1. personal hygiene and sanitation.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.
ACTIVITY 2 (Roleplay & Practice - 5 min): In small groups, pupils practice the 6-step handwashing technique using a real bar of soap and clean basins (or dry run) or roleplay brushing teeth.
ACTIVITY 3 (Surroundings Cleanup - 7 min): Pupils play a cleanup game, picking up safe trash (paper, plastic) in the classroom/schoolyard and sorting it into correct organic/inorganic bins.
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'

indicatorDescription: Observe the disappearance of mist and pools of water after rains.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: observe the disappearance of mist and pools of water after rains.

resources: Bowls of water; kettle/hot water (supervised); water-cycle chart; pictures of puddles drying up; sponge and water
keywords: observe, disappearance, mist, pools, water, rains, sun, evaporation
rpk: Learners experience day and night daily, and see rain, sun, wind, and clouds in their daily lives.
starter: Greet learners. Recite a fun weather poem together: 'Sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, we love all weather!' with physical gestures.

ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher corrects common errors on the worksheets and summarizes the natural cycle of 1. earth science.

assessment: Oral Q&A; class discussion; drawing the puddle drying up

contentStandardDescription: Recognise that different parts of the human body work interdependently to perform a specific function
indicatorDescription: Identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review, practice, and consolidate their understanding of: identify the external human body parts by their appropriate names (e.g. eyes, ears, mouth, nose, legs, hands, shoulders, knees, fingers, toes and chest).
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Human body chart; mirrors; pictures of body parts; senses-station activity (objects to feel, hear, see, smell, taste); 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' song
keywords: identify, external, human, body, parts, appropriate, names, senses
rpk: Learners are aware of their own body, hands, eyes, nose, and mouth, and use them daily.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' together with rapid physical actions.
Play 'Simon Says' to identify and touch external body parts quickly.
Recall why we need our body parts to work interdependently to play and learn.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice identifying and describing our 1. the human body systems.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Body Parts Game - 5 min): Play an accelerated game of 'Simon Says' or point to body parts to test speed and accuracy. Pupils clap for correct answers.

ACTIVITY 2 (Senses Exploration - 5 min): In small groups, pupils explore different sense objects (rough stone, smelling flower, hearing bell, tasting safely). They identify which body part is responsible.
ACTIVITY 3 (Human Body Chart - 7 min): In small groups, pupils paste labels (eyes, ears, hand, chest, shoulders, leg) onto a large blank outline of a human body.
ACTIVITY 4 (Feedback & Review - 3 min): Each group displays their body chart. Teacher provides positive feedback and reinforces vocabulary: identify, external, human.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on the next strand.
assessment: Practical body parts labeling; class exercise (classification table); Simon Says game

indicatorDescription: Explain the terms hot and cold.

ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.

Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'

contentStandardDescription: Demonstrate understanding of the components of a simple electrical circuit and their functions
indicatorDescription: Know the importance of electricity and identify common household appliances that require electricity to work.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and state the basic concepts of: know the importance of electricity and identify common household appliances that require electricity to work.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Dry cells/batteries; bulbs; wires; simple circuit kit; pictures/flashcards of household appliances (television, fridge, fan, iron)
keywords: know, importance, electricity, identify, common, household, appliances, power
rpk: Learners have played with moving toys, felt heat, and seen lights and electrical appliances at home.
starter: Greet learners. Rub hands together quickly until they feel warm. Ask: 'What do you feel? Where did the warmth come from?'
Demonstrate pushing a toy block or ball. Ask: 'Why did it move?'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we will begin learning about 2. electricity and electronics.'
Write the keyword 'know' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher demonstrates a concept. E.g., for forces, teacher pushes a chair and pulls a drawer. E.g., for simple machines, shows how a ramp (inclined plane) makes work easier.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils test pushing and pulling various classroom objects (books, bottles, blocks, pencil cases) and state whether it was a push or a pull.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Active Experiment - 7 min): In small groups, pupils explore simple sources of energy (feeling warm sunlight, safely touching warm objects, observing a glowing torch/circuit).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing - 3 min): Pupils explain their findings: 'A push moves things away, a pull brings things closer.' Teacher writes these summaries on the board.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'What did we discover today?' (Have 2-3 pupils share their findings).
Homework: 'Tell your parents or older sibling what you observed today. Show them your drawing/poster.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on DIVERSITY OF MATTER.
assessment: Practical identification of appliances; sorting worksheet; oral Q&A on uses of electricity

rpk: Learners have engaged in personal hygiene practices like bathing, handwashing, and teeth-brushing at home.
starter: Greet learners. Sing an active hygiene song like 'This is the way we wash our hands/brush our teeth.'
Do a quick 'clean fingers check' or 'teeth check' in pairs to encourage good hygiene.
Recall why keeping clean and disposing of waste is important to stay healthy.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'Today we are going to practice and show how we maintain 3. waste management.'
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Cleanliness Review - 5 min): Teacher shows pictures of dirty hands, healthy skin, clean teeth. Pupils discuss why personal hygiene keeps us healthy and free from scabies or decay.
ACTIVITY 2 (Roleplay & Practice - 5 min): In small groups, pupils practice the 6-step handwashing technique using a real bar of soap and clean basins (or dry run) or roleplay brushing teeth.
ACTIVITY 3 (Surroundings Cleanup - 7 min): Pupils play a cleanup game, picking up safe trash (paper, plastic) in the classroom/schoolyard and sorting it into correct organic/inorganic bins.
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection - 3 min): Teacher highlights the importance of clean surroundings, clean air, and clean water. Commends pupils for their cleanup work.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.

indicatorDescription: Identify and classify materials as solid, liquid or gas.

keywords: identify, classify, materials, solid, liquid, gas
rpk: Learners have seen various plants, animals, and non-living objects in their school and home environment.
starter: Greet learners warmly and sing a happy Mother-Tongue science rhyme.

NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin exploring 2. materials.'
Write the key word 'identify' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher leads a safe walk into the schoolyard or school garden. Teacher points to a living plant and a non-living stone, describing how they look and feel.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Discovery - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups with hand lenses to observe leaves, tree barks, soil, or ants. They describe their observations to their peers.
ACTIVITY 3 (Drawing & Sorting - 7 min): Pupils return to the classroom and draw 2 living things and 2 non-living things in their notebooks, coloring them.
ACTIVITY 4 (Discussion & Sharing - 3 min): Selected pupils show their drawings to the class and describe one feature. Teacher reinforces concepts using mother tongue where necessary.
plenary: Whole class sings today's theme song with active physical movements.

rpk: Learners are aware of their own body, hands, eyes, nose, and mouth, and use them daily.

Recall why we need our body parts to work interdependently to play and learn.
NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will practice identifying and describing our 1. the human body systems.'

plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).
Homework: 'Go home and show your family what we revised today. Help keep your home clean or practice your science words.'

assessment: Practical body parts labeling; class exercise (classification table); Simon Says game

starter: Greet learners warmly. Recite the active rhyme 'Push and Pull' or do a simple action song.

NEW TODAY: State today's focus: 'We will review and consolidate our understanding of 3. forces and motion.'

ACTIVITY 4 (Review & Reflection - 3 min): Teacher observes groups, asks probing questions about simple machines or forces, and corrects any misconceptions.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated science rhyme or sings today's theme song with active physical movements.
Ask: 'Who can tell me one important rule we revised today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils, especially those needing support).

assessment: Practical movement experiment; Q&A; drawing push and pull actions
